title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（浦正広研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Ura Masahiro)
teachers:
URA Masahiro
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
In this final course, students are expected summarize all of their university studies based on what they have learned thus far.
Each student will be expected to find a unique theme, think about problems, and then develop a process for proposing solutions to those problems.
Students will be expected to integrate their acquired knowledge on the technologies, sensibilities, and logical thinking skills related to media technology and media design in order to implement a project design method based on "CDIO" cycle.
advice:
The Project Design III course is based on the contents of classes from the first to third years of university studies. Hence, it is a culmination of four years of university life, in which students practice problem finding and solving techniques and build deliverables based on their teacher's advice and by using AI, IoT, data science, programming, VR, MR, 3D data, metaverse, e-learning, local (corporate) real issues and real data, and so on.
In this year-long, eight-credit class, students will work on individually selected project themes in order to achieve their desired results. To that end, proper self-management significantly affects the final results.
Students are expected to know themselves, work diligently on developing their strengths, and find ways to overcome their shortcomings.
Mastery of these techniques will surely be useful when going out into society. Students are expected to achieve their goals by working intensively towards higher objectives.
requiredKnowledge:
All prerequisite courses of this department must already be completed.
Students must be able to summarize what they have learned from the first to third years of study.
Students are expected to have mastered problem-finding and solving methods through the experiences gained in project design subjects and the specialized seminars held from the first to the third year.

activityGoals.body: Be able to acquire basic skills as a creative engineer by experiencing problem discovery and solution techniques
Be able to explain about their fields of specialization.
Be able to deepen personal insights related to engineering ethics.
Be able to apply their specialized expertise to their project themes.

lessons.content:
Students will report to each other on
the progress of their individual research themes
and the results of their study of given issues.
Students are expected to help each other improve
their respective research contents through
discussions.
Students will make presentations on and off
campus, as appropriate, in terms of results.
An intermediate review is conducted during the
7th or 8th week of the first semester.
An intermediate presentation will be made at the
end of the first semester.
(200 min * 15 weeks)
